_README: Production configuration. Secret values (ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection, JwtSettings:SecretKey, EmailSettings:Email/Password) are NOT overridden here so they are inherited from appsettings.json. Where a hosting environment supports it, override them with environment variables (section separator '__'), e.g. ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection, JwtSettings__SecretKey, EmailSettings__Password. Do NOT re-introduce empty-string values for these keys: an empty string overrides the base value and makes the app fail to start (HTTP 500.30).
_README_RateLimiting: RateLimiting is a sliding window, not the fixed window it replaced: a fixed window let a caller that spent its budget early sit blocked for the rest of the minute, and let a burst straddling the boundary through at twice the limit. SegmentsPerWindow is how many slices the window recovers in. Anonymous callers are partitioned by client address and get the larger ceiling (1200/min) precisely BECAUSE an address is a poor identity — CGNAT, campus and office networks put many real people behind one. A signed-in caller is partitioned by account instead and gets 600/min, which no human browsing session approaches, and which no other user can spend. Sign-in, registration and password reset stay at 20/min on the auth policy. QueueLimit is 0 everywhere on purpose: queueing an over-limit request buys latency and holds a connection open. Override any value with e.g. RateLimiting__Anonymous__PermitPerWindow. RateLimiting__Enabled=false disables limiting entirely and is an emergency escape hatch only. These numbers are chosen from the shape of ordinary traffic — a category page costs roughly ten requests — and are not a capacity claim.
_README_DatabaseRetry: Database:MaxRetryCount and MaxRetryDelaySeconds configure EF Core's SQL Server retry-on-failure strategy, which retries transient connection and deadlock errors. Because a retrying strategy refuses user-initiated transactions, every explicit transaction goes through IUnitOfWork.ExecuteInTransactionAsync, which runs the whole block inside the execution strategy and clears the change tracker before each attempt so a retry starts from a clean slate. Do not call BeginTransactionAsync directly. CommandTimeoutSeconds is the per-command timeout against a remote database host.
_README_Database: The connection string sets Encrypt=True, so every packet between the application and SQL Server is TLS-encrypted; it previously read Encrypt=False, which left the session in clear text. TrustServerCertificate=True is set because the managed host presents a certificate from an authority that is not publicly trusted, and strict validation fails login outright. That encrypts the wire but does NOT authenticate the server, so an attacker who can intercept the path to the database host could still impersonate it. To close that gap, either move to a provider whose certificate chains to a public CA and drop TrustServerCertificate, or pin the server certificate: export it and set ServerCertificate=/path/to/server.cer with TrustServerCertificate removed. Override the whole string in production with the environment variable ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection.
_README_AdminUser: The AdminUser section is deliberately absent here, and absent from appsettings.json. IdentityDataSeeder has no built-in fallback credentials: with the section unset it only ensures the 'Admin' role exists and seeds no account, so the local development administrator (see appsettings.Development.json) can never appear in Production. Existing administrators are unaffected. To bootstrap an administrator on a fresh Production database, set AdminUser__UserName, AdminUser__Email and AdminUser__Password as environment variables (never in a committed file), start the app once, then remove them.
_README_FrontendUrl: App:FrontendUrl is the public address of the SITE, not of this API, and it is the only thing invitation links are built from (IReferralLinkBuilder appends App:RegisterPath and the App:ReferralQueryParameter query string to it, giving https://shopiklopik.com/register?ref=CODE). It is deliberately separate from App:BaseUrl, which is the API origin used for uploaded-file URLs. The link is never derived from the incoming request, because that would send invitees to the API host. Start-up fails outside Development if this key is missing, is not an absolute http/https URL, or points at localhost.
_README_DemoData: DemoData:Enabled is false everywhere except appsettings.Development.json. The demo/sample data seeder additionally refuses to run in any environment other than Development, so a Production database is never populated with demo users, listings, workshops, craftsmen or posts. Only EF HasData reference data (categories, sub-categories, governorate/centers, module lookups, home sections, platform settings, payment methods, banner placements, admin permission pages) is seeded, and that is required for the application to function.
_README_Hosting: Production runs on Kestrel behind Nginx on Linux: 'dotnet MarkatPlace.dll'. No IIS, and no listening address is hard-coded here. Kestrel binds http://localhost:5000 by default; set ASPNETCORE_URLS (e.g. 'http://127.0.0.1:5000', or 'http://unix:/run/markatplace.sock') in the service unit to change it, and point Nginx at the same address. Set ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production. TLS is terminated by Nginx, so Kestrel needs no certificate; UseHttpsRedirection only redirects if it can resolve an HTTPS port, so let Nginx do the http->https redirect, or set ASPNETCORE_HTTPS_PORT=443 to have the application issue it. App__BaseUrl is only the fallback used when a URL is built outside an HTTP request; point it at the public https origin.
_README_ForwardedHeaders: Nginx must send X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto and (if the public host differs from the Host it proxies) X-Forwarded-Host; without X-Forwarded-Proto every generated upload URL comes out as http. Loopback is always trusted, which covers Nginx on the same host. If Nginx connects from another address (a separate host, a container network), add that address to KnownProxies or its CIDR range to KnownNetworks -- otherwise the headers are ignored, generated URLs lose https and rate limiting partitions every client onto the proxy's single IP. ForwardLimit is the number of proxies in front of the app: 1 for Nginx alone, 2 with a CDN in front of it (the CDN's egress ranges then belong in KnownNetworks). TrustAnyProxy:true honours the headers from any caller and is only safe when something upstream strips client-supplied X-Forwarded-* headers.
_README_GoogleAuth: GoogleAuth:ClientId is a PUBLIC value and is committed in appsettings.json; the frontend sends it to Google anyway. GoogleAuth:ClientSecret is NOT committed anywhere and must be supplied as the environment variable GoogleAuth__ClientSecret. The secret is only needed for the authorization-code exchange (POST /api/auth/google with a code); the default frontend flow posts an idToken, which is verified against Google's public keys and needs no secret. Never place the secret in a committed file, and never return it from an endpoint: /api/auth/google/config publishes only enabled and clientId. Set GoogleAuth__RequireVerifiedEmail=false only if you accept accounts whose Google e-mail is unverified, and GoogleAuth__LinkVerifiedEmailToExistingAccount=false to refuse linking a Google account to an existing password account that shares its verified e-mail.
_README_Cors: Cors:AllowedOrigins is the browser origin allow-list; it replaces the former AllowAnyOrigin policy. Every origin the site is served from must be listed (apex and www are different origins), otherwise the browser blocks the call. Add one with Cors__AllowedOrigins__0=https://example.com (indexes REPLACE the committed array element at that index, so re-list the existing entries too). Cors__AllowAnyOrigin=true is an emergency escape hatch that restores the old permissive behaviour without a redeploy; it also disables credentialed requests. Uploaded files under /uploads are served with their own Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * header and are unaffected.
